12.t: Working with data: action and reaction
q: In test 1, what do you notice about the speeds?
They are equal (1.2 m/s each), in opposite directions.
State Newton’s third law using this push.
When A pushes B, B pushes A with an equal force in the opposite direction.
Predict the speed of B in test 3.
B is twice as heavy as A, so it moves at half the speed: 1.0 m/s.
Explain why the lighter student always moves faster, though the forces are equal.
Equal forces, but a = F / m: the smaller mass gets a bigger acceleration during the push, so it reaches a higher speed.
